Title: Category and priority rules
Statement: Apply the exact four category-to-route mappings and evaluate Critical, High, Medium, then Low in fixed order so the first satisfied level controls.
Configuration_Rule: Category routes: Access or permission->Access/Permissions; Application or workflow issue->Application/Workflow; Data or reporting request->Data/Reporting; General service request->General Service. Priority precedence: Evaluate Critical, then High, then Medium, then Low; the first satisfied level controls. Critical=fully blocked, no workaround, immediate action; High=multiple users or time-sensitive commitment materially affected, or one requester fully blocked without workaround; Medium=workaround available or near-term requested-by window; Low=informational, routine, minor enhancement, or no near-term impact.
Expected_Result: The representative Data or reporting request is not Critical or High, first satisfies Medium, and repeatedly routes to Data/Reporting.
Assumptions: Priority precedence and all four category routes are frozen and platform-neutral.
Notes: No platform configuration is claimed.

Once assigned, exactly one Fulfiller is accountable. Reassignment requires a reason and leaves exactly one current accountable Fulfiller.
Expected_Result: With no matching skill, state remains Submitted and the coordinator retains coordination; assignment and every reasoned reassignment leave exactly one current accountable Fulfiller.
Assumptions: A fictional matching Fulfiller becomes available during the modeled path.
Notes: Collaboration does not create a fifth role.
